skills/toil/bitbucket-cloud.md

Repositories, branches and tags, commits, diffs, files, pull requests, comments, build statuses and Pipelines on Bitbucket Cloud (https://api.bitbucket.org/2.0, REST API 2.0). Built from Atlassian’s API documentation and never run against a live workspace. Verification level: unit.

For Bitbucket Data Center or Server, use the bitbucket area instead. The two are separate areas because their APIs differ: Cloud has workspaces where Data Center has projects, identifies people by Atlassian account id rather than username, keeps no pull request version, and pages by a next link.

Supported versions: The oldest Bitbucket Cloud version toil supports hasn’t been established. Bitbucket Cloud is always current. toil calls REST API 2.0 (https://api.bitbucket.org/2.0) with an Atlassian API token sent as Basic auth with the account email, or a workspace, project or repository access token sent as Bearer. Nothing has been run against a live workspace yet.

Credential

One of two, each generated once in Atlassian’s UI. A connection holds exactly one; setting both is refused with CONFIG_INVALID.

  • An Atlassian API token with Bitbucket scopes, plus that account’s email address. Create it at https://id.atlassian.com/manage-profile/security/api-tokens → Create API token with scopes → Bitbucket. toil sends Authorization: Basic base64(<email>:<apiToken>), as Atlassian documents. The token acts as you. Scopes:
    • reads: read:repository:bitbucket, read:pullrequest:bitbucket and read:pipeline:bitbucket, plus read:user:bitbucket for toil connections test
    • writes: write:pullrequest:bitbucket (pull requests and comments), write:repository:bitbucket (create-branch, create-tag) and admin:repository:bitbucket (create-repo)
  • A workspace, project or repository access token, from Repository settings, Project settings or Workspace settings → Access tokens. toil sends Authorization: Bearer <accessToken>. The token acts as itself, named after the token, on only what it was made for. Scopes: repository, pullrequest and pipeline to read; pullrequest:write and repository:write to write. toil connections test checks it against the connection’s workspace and repo, and can’t check one with neither.

App passwords no longer work and toil doesn’t take them. A 401, 403 or 410 from Bitbucket Cloud is AUTH, and its fix names the credential to create and the scopes it needs. There is no OAuth app, Connect app or browser login.

Configuration

KeyEnv varRequiredMeaning
baseUrlTOIL_BITBUCKET_CLOUD_BASE_URLyesREST API root: https://api.bitbucket.org/2.0
emailTOIL_BITBUCKET_CLOUD_EMAILwith apiTokenEmail address of the Atlassian account the API token belongs to
apiTokenTOIL_BITBUCKET_CLOUD_API_TOKENone of the twoAtlassian API token with Bitbucket scopes (a secret)
accessTokenTOIL_BITBUCKET_CLOUD_ACCESS_TOKENone of the twoWorkspace, project or repository access token (a secret)
workspaceTOIL_BITBUCKET_CLOUD_WORKSPACEnoDefault workspace slug, when --ws isn’t given
repoTOIL_BITBUCKET_CLOUD_REPOnoDefault repository slug, when --repo isn’t given
writesTOIL_BITBUCKET_CLOUD_WRITESnotrue lets write commands run (with --allow-write)

CI fallback: in Bitbucket Pipelines, the default connection takes workspace from BITBUCKET_WORKSPACE and repo from BITBUCKET_REPO_SLUG, which Pipelines sets on every step, when TOIL_BITBUCKET_CLOUD_WORKSPACE and TOIL_BITBUCKET_CLOUD_REPO aren’t set. Pipelines sets no API credential, so the token is still yours to supply as a secured variable.

export TOIL_BITBUCKET_CLOUD_BASE_URL=https://api.bitbucket.org/2.0
export TOIL_BITBUCKET_CLOUD_EMAIL=you@example.com
export TOIL_BITBUCKET_CLOUD_API_TOKEN=<your API token>
# or, instead of the two above:
export TOIL_BITBUCKET_CLOUD_ACCESS_TOKEN=<your access token>

Or ~/.toil/config.json, with workspace and repo usually set once under defaults.bitbucket-cloud:

{
  "version": 2,
  "connections": {
    "imagile-bbc": { "area": "bitbucket-cloud", "baseUrl": "https://api.bitbucket.org/2.0", "email": "you@example.com", "writes": true }
  },
  "defaults": { "bitbucket-cloud": { "connection": "imagile-bbc", "workspace": "imagile", "repo": "toil" } }
}

Neither token ever goes in this file; a plaintext one there is refused with CONFIG_INVALID. Run toil connections add imagile-bbc --area bitbucket-cloud (or toil connections login imagile-bbc) to keep it in the OS credential store, or set the env var. Env vars always win over the file.

Workspace and repository

Every command takes --ws <slug> and --repo <slug>, before or after the command name: toil bitbucket-cloud --ws imagile --repo toil list-prs. It’s --ws, not --workspace, because toil’s own --workspace is the folder commands may read and write files in. Each falls back to a dossier, then the connection’s workspace and repo. The git remote is not read. list-repos and create-repo need only the workspace; everything else needs both. Over MCP they’re the workspace and repo fields.

Commands

Every command also takes --connection <name>. Write commands (marked ✎) need writes: true on the connection and --allow-write. Names and flags match bitbucket wherever the operation is the same. MCP tools are bitbucket_cloud_<command> (bitbucket_cloud_get_pr). delete-comment is CLI only: it is never an MCP tool.

People

Bitbucket Cloud has no usernames in its API. --reviewers takes a comma-separated list of Atlassian account ids (557058:abc12345-…), or {uuid}s in braces, as get-pr and list-default-reviewers show them. list-prs --query filters with Bitbucket’s query language, for example --query 'author.account_id = "557058:abc12345"' or --query 'source.branch.name = "feature/retries"', where bitbucket had --author and --reviewer.

Paging

Lists follow Bitbucket’s next link, 100 items a request, and toil follows a link only when it’s on the connection’s own host and names the same list. Without --limit, list-repos, list-branches, list-tags and list-prs read every page; list-commits and list-pipelines return the newest 100, since a history has no end worth reaching. With --limit N they return at most N, and meta.page.nextCursor resumes: pass it back as --cursor (with --limit on the lists that read every page). Every other list is read in full. Paging stops after 1,000 requests with an error naming the list.

Any endpoint: bitbucket-cloud api

When no command above covers an endpoint, bitbucket-cloud api calls it directly. It sends the connection’s own credential, the same way every other bitbucket-cloud command does, to a path under the connection’s baseUrl (so the path starts after /2.0):

toil bitbucket-cloud api GET repositories/imagile/toil
toil bitbucket-cloud api GET repositories/imagile/toil/refs/branches --query 'q=name ~ "release"' --query pagelen=10
toil bitbucket-cloud api GET repositories/imagile/toil/pullrequests/42/merge/task-status/abc12345
toil bitbucket-cloud api POST repositories/imagile/toil/pullrequests/42/comments --body-file comment.json --allow-write
  • The path is relative to baseUrl, with or without a leading / (in Git Bash on Windows, leave it off: the shell rewrites /repositories/... into a file path, which is refused). A full URL, a scheme, //host, a leading backslash or a . / .. segment is refused with INVALID_INPUT before anything is sent, so the token never leaves the connection’s host.
  • The method decides the gate. GET and HEAD are reads. POST, PUT, PATCH and DELETE are writes: they need writes: true on the connection and --allow-write. DELETE works only on the CLI: over MCP, bitbucket_cloud_api refuses it with INVALID_INPUT.
  • --query key=value adds a query parameter; repeat it for more, or to repeat a key. --body-file <path> sends that file (inside the workspace, or - for stdin) as the body, as application/json unless --content-type says otherwise.
  • Output: a JSON body is data, parsed. A text body (text/*, XML, or no content type) is data as text. Any other body is binary: data is its bytes as base64, with an API_BINARY warning. Text and binary are capped at 1 MB, with an API_TRUNCATED warning when the body was longer. An empty body (a 204, a HEAD) is null. meta.response is { status, contentType }. Errors use the usual codes (AUTH, NOT_FOUND, HTTP, NETWORK) with Bitbucket’s own message; a 410 here is AUTH, as it is on every other command. A body labelled JSON that doesn’t parse comes back as text, with an API_NOT_JSON warning.
  • Over MCP it’s the bitbucket_cloud_api tool, with method, path, query (an array of key=value strings), bodyFile, contentType and allowWrite.

Prefer a wrapped command when one exists: it knows the endpoint’s paging and quirks, and bitbucket-cloud api doesn’t.

Notes

  • get-file and list-dir read at --ref, a branch, tag or commit hash (the repository’s main branch without it). A branch or tag is first resolved to its newest commit, which data.commit reports, so a branch name with a / works. A file comes back as text; read a folder with list-dir, not get-file.
  • diff --pr and list-files read the pull request first and diff its source commit against its destination with topic=true, the three-dot diff Bitbucket shows on the pull request, so --file and --context-lines apply. diff --spec takes one commit (against its first parent) or a..b. Pass exactly one of --pr and --spec. A pull request from a fork isn’t diffed this way: use --spec in the fork, or api.
  • update-pr reads the pull request first and sends back its current title, description and reviewers for anything not given, so nothing is cleared by omission. --reviewers replaces the whole list.
  • merge-pr --delete-branch sends close_source_branch, which deletes the source branch after the merge. --strategy is one of merge_commit, squash, fast_forward, squash_fast_forward, rebase_fast_forward or rebase_merge; left out, the repository’s default applies. When Bitbucket queues the merge or takes longer than it waits (202), data is { pending: true, taskStatus } with a BITBUCKET_CLOUD_MERGE_PENDING warning: read taskStatus with bitbucket-cloud api GET until its task_status is SUCCESS.
  • request-changes is Cloud’s needs-work. unapprove withdraws an approval. Adding a single reviewer is update-pr --reviewers with the whole list.
  • add-inline-comment anchors ADDED and CONTEXT lines in the new file (to) and REMOVED lines in the old one (from).
  • resolve-comment takes the thread’s root comment; one that’s already resolved is an HTTP 409.
  • current-pr matches the current git branch against open pull requests’ source branch. It reads the branch from .git, and the workspace and repository from --ws and --repo or the connection, never from the remote.
  • get-step-log follows a redirect to signed storage with every header dropped, so the credential stays on baseUrl’s host. Pipeline and step uuids are taken with or without their braces.
  • Not covered: Issues and Wikis (removed from Bitbucket Cloud in August 2026), the cross-workspace APIs (retired in April 2026), anything only a Connect app can reach, starting or stopping a pipeline, and deleting branches, tags or repositories.
  • A 429 is retried after the delay Bitbucket asks for, as in every area.

Settings at a glance

  • baseUrl required

    Bitbucket Cloud REST API root: https://api.bitbucket.org/2.0

    TOIL_BITBUCKET_CLOUD_BASE_URL

  • email

    Email address of the Atlassian account an API token belongs to (with apiToken)

    TOIL_BITBUCKET_CLOUD_EMAIL

  • apiToken secret

    Atlassian API token with Bitbucket scopes, sent as Basic auth with email

    TOIL_BITBUCKET_CLOUD_API_TOKEN

  • accessToken secret

    Workspace, project or repository access token, sent as Bearer

    TOIL_BITBUCKET_CLOUD_ACCESS_TOKEN

  • workspace

    Default workspace slug

    TOIL_BITBUCKET_CLOUD_WORKSPACE orBITBUCKET_WORKSPACE

  • repo

    Default repository slug

    TOIL_BITBUCKET_CLOUD_REPO orBITBUCKET_REPO_SLUG
